subject: Mutual action checklist & next steps from today's discovery call
messages:
--- Message 1 (original) ---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>
To: Amelia Thompson <amelia@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual action checklist & next steps from today's discovery call

Amelia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed mutual action checklist so we have alignment on milestones, owners, and dates. I kept this tight so it can slot into your procurement timeline.

Pain / goals we heard (your words):
- High throughput inference across mixed workloads (EHR summarization + real-time triage) at predictable unit cost.
- Data residency for PHI workflows (on-prem or VPC) and audited access logs for regulators.
- Minimal disruption to existing latency-sensitive endpoints (p95 < 120ms goal).

Proposed mutual action checklist (first pass):
1) Executive buy-in & scope signoff
   - Owner: Amelia (Orion) / Karthik (Redwood)
   - Target: 2026-09-30
2) Security questionnaire & evidence exchange (SOC2, data flow diagrams)
   - Owner: Rajesh (Orion) / Marissa (Redwood)
messages_2:
- Target: 2026-10-07
3) Technical POC design & success criteria
   - Owner: Sophie (Orion) / Dev (Redwood)
   - Deliverable: 2-week POC plan, test prompts, latency/cost baselines
   - Target start: 2026-10-12; complete: 2026-10-26
4) Private deployment scoping (VPC/networking + KMS)
   - Owner: Rajesh (Orion) / Dev (Redwood)
   - Target: 2026-10-20 (network design approval)
5) Contracting & SLA discussion (exceptions noted)
   - Owner: Amelia (Orion) / Karthik (Redwood legal ops)
   - Target: 2026-10-28

Open questions we flagged (need answers to finalize the MAP):
- Which regions must stay on-prem vs. acceptable cloud regions?
- Expected average vs. peak tokens per request for triage workloads?
- Any vendor security attestations beyond SOC2 that procurement requires?

Attachments: I attached a stubbed Mutual Action Plan (ORH-Map-v1.xlsx) and a draft of the SLA exceptions we discussed.

Next steps from Redwood: I'll drop a filled MAP into the shared Drive and send the updated plan once I have the region/volume answers. Can you confirm the executive signoff owner and whether procurement requires an SSO onboarding checklist?

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.inference.com

--- Message 2 (external reply) ---
From: Amelia Thompson <amelia@orionhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Rajesh Nair <rajesh.nair@orionhealth.com>, Sophie Lu <sophie.lu@orionhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Mutual action checklist & next steps from today's discovery call

Thanks Karthik — very clear. Quick answers and one update:
- Executive owner: I will own scope signoff but need CIO-level visibility; I'll loop in Noah King if we get to contracting.
- Regions: US-only for PHI workloads; non-PHI can run in EU.
- Avg tokens: triage ~600 tokens/request avg, peaks ~2k during shift changes.
- Procurement asks for FedRAMP equivalency note and confirmation on log retention duration (we keep logs for 7 years).

We reviewed the MAP and added a legal review gate before contracting — can Redwood share any precedent exceptions you have accepted (high level)?

Sophie will be our POC for the technical proof of concept. We'll aim to have scope signoff by 9/30 but procurement can be slower depending on legal.

—Amelia
VP Product Operations, Orion Health

I'll push a POC outline to the shared Drive by EOD Friday (9/18).

Dev
